# Generated files and adopted workflows

Covers: crates/core/src/engine/generated_paths.rs, crates/core/src/engine/generated_paths/, crates/core/src/attest.rs, crates/core/src/commit_offer/, crates/cli/src/commands/verify.rs, crates/core/src/tracked_output.rs

The inventory records files that verification can compare with declared content. A verification record does not grant permission to overwrite or restore a file.

## Boundaries

- Verification reads source mirrors offline. A recorded commit absent from its mirror fails history and stale render rows with `fix="kendex source refresh"`. A held commit outside the declared history still fails as off-history. Enforced by `crates/cli/tests/verify_records.rs::a_mirror_behind_the_record_names_source_refresh_and_recovers` and `crates/cli/tests/verify_at_record.rs`.
- CI reads the committed generated-file inventory from the render plan. In-place sources and Pi carrier payloads stay outside it. Enforced by `crates/core/tests/instruction_shims.rs::generated_inventory_tracks_renders_and_excludes_source` and the harness-ci package tests.
- A skill's render leaves out the package's top-level `tests/`, `evals/` and `DEVELOPMENT.md`. Agents do not read them at run time, and a consumer does not run a package's tests. The inventory lists none of them. `SealedSource::rendered_item` is the one reading of which files an install holds: the render, the source and render hashes in the lock, the catalog check, the browse preview, the package page, the package diff and the import wizard's edited-copy test all take it. An edit to one of these entries moves no source or render hash in a consumer's lock; only the recorded source commit advances, as for any catalog commit. A refresh replaces the skill's tree whole, which deletes the copies an earlier render wrote. A copy of the package (detach, templates, the bytes an import writes) keeps the whole tree, and a fork holds the rendered files only. A template or example deeper in the tree that carries one of these names is still rendered. `tools/guard`'s render rule owes no render for the same entries. Enforced by `crates/core/src/source_read/tests.rs::a_rendered_skill_tree_leaves_out_top_level_tests_evals_and_development_notes` and `::guard_not_rendered_is_the_render_list`, `crates/core/src/hash/tests.rs::an_edit_a_render_leaves_out_moves_no_installation_hash`, `crates/cli/tests/refresh_fresh_clone.rs::a_refresh_removes_the_tests_an_earlier_render_wrote`, and the change-class row `a refresh that drops rendered tests/ is a render`.
- Apply records rendered paths in the inventory. Package adoption commands also declare workflow copies there, with a template path and SHA-256 hash. The writer and `crates/core/src/engine/generated_paths/own_inventory.rs` use one selected set and document from `GeneratedPaths`: written positions, adoption declarations, and held positions already listed at `HEAD`. Existing held files remain outside the commit offer. Enforced by `crates/cli/tests/refresh_fresh_clone.rs::a_stale_committed_skill_keeps_its_inventory_with_or_without_a_lock` and `crates/core/tests/instruction_shims.rs::refused_outputs_stay_out_of_inventory_and_later_ownership`.
- A pull request leaves the install record as `main` holds it, so no pull-request check fails on what `kendex verify` reports about its renders: [D007](../decisions/D007-lock-record-on-main.md) removed the record row, and the change-class render proof only picks a lane class. `crates/core/src/engine/generated_paths/own_renders.rs` plans a copy of what a commit of this checkout carries with edits discarded, and fails on each inventory path but the record that a planned op lands on, directly or through a tree holding it. It names apart each the plan holds back, a file kendex did not write with other bytes or a conflict, which settling the row the refresh reports clears. The copy keeps every held position, including the render of a package the branch adds that the inventory at `HEAD` does not list. A render synced by hand to other bytes than its source renders, a render tree holding a file the render does not write, a deleted nested `CLAUDE.md` shim, or a hand edit to a hook registration in a shared settings file would otherwise land, and the refresh after the merge would keep it as an edit that fails verify on `main`. Enforced by `crates/core/src/engine/generated_paths/own_renders.rs::the_committed_renders_are_the_bytes_this_checkout_renders`, `::a_render_its_source_no_longer_renders_is_refused`, `::a_render_of_a_package_the_record_does_not_hold_is_refused`, `::a_render_tree_holding_a_file_it_does_not_render_is_refused` and `::a_nested_instruction_shim_deleted_is_refused`.
- `GeneratedPaths::beside` names every file a write can change beside its renders without kendex owning it whole: the manifest, `kendex.settings.toml`, `.gitignore` and the shared edit targets. The app's reading before a write takes it as that write's files, since the app cannot see the write's plan; the terminal takes the paths its plan touches. A restore takes none of them: it plans over the files kendex owns whole alone, and `crates/core/src/commit_offer/tests.rs::putting_a_render_back_never_writes_over_the_manifest` enforces it for the manifest. A commit carries one only where the action changed it from a clean state (`commit_offer::Scan::carry`), enforced by `::what_a_commit_carries_beside_the_renders_is_one_answer_every_reader_takes`. One deletion rule in `commit_offer::paths::sort` serves every reader, the reading before an action and the passive scan alike: a deleted path the committed inventory names is kendex's whole, so a removal commits the deletion of a render the person edited, unless `GeneratedPaths::beside` names it. A shared edit target the plan edits or empties and takes away (`GeneratedPaths::edited`), or one the install record at `HEAD` writes keys in (`GeneratedPaths::recorded`), is never owned whole, so an uncommitted removal's emptied settings file stays out of whole-file commit and restore. Gemini's instruction shim is a shared edit target, a key in `.gemini/settings.json`, and `GeneratedPaths::recorded` takes that file as one where the record at `HEAD` keeps the shim (`lock::Lock::shims`) or, where that record lacks it, the inventory at `HEAD` lists the file. The retirement takes the shim on the same evidence on disk, one rule for both (`engine::instruction_shims::recorded_shims`). Enforced by `crates/core/tests/instruction_shims.rs::a_persons_key_beside_the_gemini_shim_stays_out_of_commit_and_restore` and `::a_gemini_shim_written_before_the_record_was_kept_is_recorded_then_retired`. Where `HEAD` holds a record this build does not read, or none while its inventory lists paths (`Recorded::Unknown`), the rule claims only a deletion the record on disk names as a whole-file render, so a deletion it cannot place stays out of the commit and is named; planning never fails over the copy at `HEAD`. Enforced by `crates/cli/tests/commit_offer_cli.rs::a_remove_commits_the_deletion_of_a_render_the_person_edited`, `::a_remove_commits_a_shared_file_it_edits_and_leaves_out_one_the_person_emptied` and `::a_passive_reading_keeps_a_deleted_shared_file_out_of_the_renders`.
- Adopted workflow equality uses template bytes from declared package artifacts. An edited installed template cannot attest an edited workflow. Refresh records the expected hash but never rewrites or restores the workflow. An invalid inventory retains its bytes so apply cannot erase unreadable adoption declarations. Enforced by `crates/cli/tests/verify_adopted_workflows.rs` under [D003](../decisions/D003-one-merge-path.md).
- `Output::at_record` in `crates/cli/src/commands/verify.rs` owns which revision each verify reading takes a template at. A copy that differs is a failed row naming the template's revision where its source has one, the copy's hash, the template's hash and the package whose adoption step copies it again. The closing line counts it after the lock entries. Enforced by `crates/core/src/engine/generated_paths/adopted/tests.rs` and `crates/cli/tests/verify_adopted_workflows.rs::a_copy_left_behind_by_a_revision_bump_fails_the_plain_project_scope`.
- A path an enabled agent the project installs declares in its `tracked-outputs` frontmatter that the project ignores is a `verify` warning row naming the agent, the path and the ignore rule. The closing line counts it apart from every failure and the run stays clean, because a project may keep an agent's output local on purpose; under `--strict` the row fails and counts after the lock entries. `crates/core/src/tracked_output.rs` asks git, and a git that cannot answer fails the run either way. The global scope has no repository and is not asked. Enforced by `crates/cli/tests/verify_tracked_outputs.rs`, whose rows cover the ignored path with and without `--strict`, the tracked one, the path git cannot judge and the review-gate consumer refresh's own verify line, and `crates/core/src/tracked_output.rs::a_path_git_cannot_judge_is_an_error`.
- A hook's `harnesses` pin, on a declaration or a `[[custom-hooks]]` entry and whether the hook is switched on or off, that leaves out a tool kendex would write the hook to with no pin, its required companions running there too, or names a tool the hook's own harnesses line excludes, is a `verify` row in state `notice` naming the hook, the tool and the remedy: drop the pin, or change that tool's place in it. The engine's skip decision is the one source (`EngineReport::pinned_hooks`), and the run stays clean, `--strict` included. Enforced by `crates/cli/tests/verify_hook_pins.rs`.
